# How to enable curl in Wamp server

If you are troubleshooting a missing `curl` extension in WampServer despite trying every standard forum answer, it is usually because the approach focuses on file placement rather than PHP configuration. The error stems from PHP not loading the extension at runtime, regardless of whether the `.dll` file exists in the system directories or if you have commented out lines in a config file.

To resolve this, you must understand how WampServer manages PHP versions and extensions. Unlike a standard Linux environment where you might manually edit `/etc/php/8.x/apache2/php.ini`, WampServer bundles multiple PHP distributions to support backward compatibility. The most common pitfall is editing the wrong `php.ini` file or assuming that uncommenting a line in a global configuration file affects a specific version used by your application.

### Verifying the Extension Load Status

Before modifying any files, confirm whether the extension is actually being loaded for the specific PHP version your project requires. Open WampServer and check the "Web Server" menu to select the PHP version you intend to use (e.g., 8.1 or 7.4). Then, access a file named `info.php` in your document root containing:

```php
<?php phpinfo(); ?>
```

Search the resulting page for "curl". If the section is missing entirely, PHP has not loaded the extension. If it is present but disabled, look for the line `extension=curl` under the `[PHP Modules]` or `[Loaded Extensions]` sections. Note that on Windows, this setting often appears as `extension=php_curl.dll`.

### The Correct File Location and Edit

The source material mentions copying `php_curl.dll` into the "win sistem," which is a frequent misunderstanding. You do not install DLLs directly into the system folder (`C:\Windows\System32`). Instead, you must place the extension in the PHP-specific extensions directory. For WampServer, this path typically looks like:

`[WAMP_DIR]\www\php\ext` or `[WAMP_DIR]\wamp\bin\php\phpXYZ\ext`

Depending on your Wamp version and PHP setup, the structure might vary slightly. Once inside the correct `ext` folder, ensure that `php_curl.dll` is present. If you are using a custom PHP distribution provided by Wamp, verify that the DLL matches the architecture (usually x86-64 for modern systems).

Next, locate the active configuration file. In WampServer, this is often found at:
`[WAMP_DIR]\wamp\php\phpXYZ\php.ini-production` or a similarly named `php.ini-development`.

Edit this specific file and ensure the line reads:
```ini
extension=curl
```
Remove any leading semicolon (`;`) if it exists. Avoid editing `php.ini-development` unless you are intentionally developing with that configuration, as production environments should rely on `php.ini-production` to prevent accidental changes from persisting in unintended ways.

### Handling Multiple PHP Versions

A critical nuance in WampServer is the coexistence of multiple PHP versions. If your project requires PHP 8.1 but the default server is running PHP 7.4, editing the global config or the wrong version's config will yield no results. Use the dropdown in the WampSystem tray to switch between versions and verify which `php.ini` corresponds to the active web server configuration. You can inspect this by running `php --ini` from a command line after switching versions in the tray.

### Troubleshooting DLL Loading Errors

If you have verified the file exists, the extension is loaded in `info.php`, but your application still fails with "curl function not found," check for version mismatches between the PHP core and the extension. Sometimes, WampServer updates the PHP core without updating the bundled extensions. In such cases, simply copying a DLL from another machine or an online source often breaks the binary compatibility.

Instead of manually copying files into the system drive, rely on WampServer's built-in update mechanism to refresh the PHP stack if necessary. Additionally, ensure that no other conflicting `php.ini` files are being loaded via `.user.ini` or Apache-specific overrides that might be overriding your extension settings.

For developers transitioning from a Linux environment to WampServer, remember that the directory structure and version management differ significantly. While https://laravelcompany.com offers insights into modern PHP stack configurations, the core principle remains: match the extension path and configuration file to the exact PHP binary currently serving your requests.
